national_raw_news.content: Marking a new chapter in Indian cinema, President Droupadi Murmu will present the historic 72nd National Film Awards this evening at Ekta Nagar. Instituted in 1954, these awards represent India’s highest cinematic honours, recognising artistic and technical excellence across various categories, namely Feature, Non-Feature, and Writing on Cinema. As part of a major policy initiative by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the awards are being held outside the national capital. The ceremony at Ekta Nagar brings together cinematic talent from across the country, embodying the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’. The president will also honour the veteran actor Anant Nag with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024. The stage is set, and the lights are ready in the iconic Ekta Nagar as Kevadia prepares to host the historic 72nd National Film Awards for the very first time. Renowned actors, acclaimed filmmakers, and technicians from across the country have started arriving at the venue for this grand celebration of Indian cinema. The ceremony honours outstanding cinematic achievements for the year 2024. Among the major feature film announcements, Article 370 was selected for Best Feature Film, with Yami Gautam winning Best Actress for her role in the film. The Best Actor honour is shared by Mammootty for Bramayugam and Kartik Aaryan for Chandu Champion. Rajkumar Periasamy earned Best Direction for Amaran, while Kalki 2898 AD was named Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Randeep Hooda won Best Debut Director for Swatantrya Veer Savarkar. In the non-feature category, the Marathi film Bhangaar was named Best Non-Feature Film, while Director Aanand L Rai was selected for Best Direction for Statue of Unity – Ekta ka Prateek. Ravi Raj Murmu took the Best Debut Director (Non-Feature) honour for the Santhali film, Angen.

national_raw_news.title: 50 mins ago | National 144 EAM S Jaishankar holds talks with France, Ecuador, Slovakia, Switzerland counterparts in New York
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar held talks with his counterparts from France, Ecuador, Slovakia and Switzerland on the sidelines of UN General Assembly in New York last night and discussed regional and global issues. Mr Jaishankar arrived in New York City on Sunday, leading the Indian delegation for the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. Mr Jaishankar will address world leaders at the General Debate from the UNGA podium on September 26. His engagements commenced with a meeting with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot. In a social media post Mr Jaishankar said the regular meetings and telecons enable both countries to maintain the momentum of Special Global Strategic Partnership. He said that during the meeting, regional and global issues, specifically the Ukraine and Gulf crises, were discussed. Both the leaders also exchanged views on multilateral issues, including the reform of UN Security Council. External Affairs Minister also held a meeting with Ecuador Foreign Minister Roberto Kury, to strengthen economic ties, including energy and pharmaceuticals, mobility, training of personnel, development partnership and cooperation in multilateral fora, including the United Nations. Following his meeting with Slovakia Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar, the External Affairs Minister said that besides discussing the bilateral agenda, they also touched upon ways to deepen our multilateral cooperation. Mr. Jaishankar also held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Hungary Anita Orban. Both the leaders have agreed to work together to deepen ties to advance the bilateral strategic partnership. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held separate meetings with Switzerland Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis and Nauru President David Adeang, discussing bilateral ties, economic cooperation, and multilateral issues. Sharing details of his meeting on a social media post , Mr Jaishankar said the two sides reviewed the progress in their economic relationship following the entry into force of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement. Earlier, Dr Jaishankar attended the first Visegrád Group (V4) and India Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, involving Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic.

national_raw_news.title: Sikkim’s natural farming journey reflects PM Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat 1 hour ago 26
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Apart from mystic lakes and snow-capped mountains, Sikkim is famous for its vast agricultural offerings not only in India but also to the world. Sikkim has been declared the 1st Organic State in 2016 and is famous for crops like large cardamom, ginger buckwheat etc. Sikkim produces around 90% of large cardamom, which is Highest Large Cardamom in India, and exported to countries like Australia and the UAE. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Beema Yojana has played a pivotal role in the natural farming scenario in Sikkim. Apart from Large Cardamom, Buckwheat is one of the crops that’s extensively harvested in Sikkim which is around 1600kg per hector. Being the 3rd largest crop and 2nd most common cereal crop in Sikkim Buckwheat has a GI Certification. With time and with firm collaboration with Govt of India, ICAR Sikkim and Department of Agriculture, Govt of Sikkim the scene of Natural Farming as well as Organic Farming is growing stronger in Sikkim.

national_raw_news.title: Jharkhand celebrates Karam festival with cultural programmes and traditional rituals 3 hours ago 55
national_raw_news.content: Karam festival, a vibrant celebration of Jharkhand’s rich tribal culture, nature and the bond between brothers and sisters, is being observed across the state today with traditional fervour and enthusiasm. Special cultural and state-level programmes are being organised across Jharkhand to mark the auspicious occasion. Karam festival, one of the most significant celebrations of Jharkhand’s folk culture and nature worship, is being celebrated across the state today with great enthusiasm. Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar attended the program on the eve of Karam festival organised in Bero, Ranchi, as the chief guest and extended greetings to the people of the state. He also delivered a message on nature conservation. Yesterday, a seminar-cum-cultural programme was organised at Audrey House in Ranchi, where the entire premises came alive with Jharkhand’s cultural spirit to the beats of drums, nagadas and mandar, accompanied by traditional Karam songs. A programme was also organised yesterday evening at the Deekshant Mandap in Morabadi, where a tribal fashion show was the main attraction. Karam festival is considered a symbol of crop protection, respect for nature, and the enduring bond between brothers and sisters. On this occasion, sisters observe a Nirjala fast, praying for the well-being and long life of their brothers. This evening, a sacred branch of the Karam tree will be installed at the akhara, followed by community dances and traditional songs throughout the night. In Ranchi, the state capital, as well as in various parts of the state, arrangements have been made for cleanliness, lighting, drinking water and other essential civic facilities at Karam worship sites and akharas. Administrative officials have also reviewed preparations for the Karam festival and have participated in various events.
